title: Dialogue Writing (Part III)
instructions: Write a dialogue of at least six exchanges between a librarian and a student who wants to borrow a book that is already issued to someone else.
sample_answer:
Student   : Good morning, madam. I am looking for 'The Wings of Fire'.
Librarian : Good morning. Let me check. I am sorry, that copy was issued yesterday.
Student   : Oh. When will it be returned, madam?
Librarian : It is due on the twenty-fifth. Shall I reserve it for you?
Student   : Yes, please. My project is due at the end of the month.
Librarian : Then let me suggest something. We have a shorter biography of Dr. Kalam on the same shelf.
Student   : That would help me start, madam. May I borrow it today?
Librarian : Certainly. Please sign here, and I will send you a message when the other book comes back.
Student   : Thank you very much, madam.
Librarian : You are welcome. Do return it within a fortnight.

title: Process Description (Part III)
instructions: Describe the process of preparing filter coffee in about 80 words. Use the passive voice and sequence words such as first, then, next, after that and finally.
sample_answer: Filter coffee is prepared in a simple but careful sequence. First, two spoons of freshly ground coffee powder are placed in the upper chamber of the stainless steel filter and pressed down gently with the disc. Then boiling water is poured over it and the lid is closed. The filter is left undisturbed for about fifteen minutes, during which the decoction collects drop by drop in the lower chamber. Next, milk is boiled separately and sweetened with sugar. After that, one part of decoction is mixed with three parts of hot milk. Finally, the coffee is poured between a tumbler and a dabara several times until a thick froth is formed, and it is served hot.

title: Note-Making and Summary Writing (Part IV)
instructions: Read the passage 'The Water Crisis in Tamil Nadu' in the Reading section. Make notes on it using a title, headings, sub-headings and recognisable abbreviations, and then write a summary of about 80 words.
sample_answer:
TITLE: WATER CRISIS IN TAMIL NADU

1. The problem
   1.1 Rain from NE monsoon, Oct-Dec
   1.2 Falls in heavy bursts, runs off to sea
   1.3 Shortage is of storage, not rainfall

2. Traditional system
   2.1 Temple tanks, ooranis, channels
   2.2 Each tank caught rain from small catchment
   2.3 Slowly recharged nearby wells

3. What went wrong
   3.1 Tanks built over or silted up
   3.2 Borewells replaced tanks
   3.3 Pumping faster than recharge -> aquifer depletion

4. A working remedy
   4.1 Chennai rainwater harvesting compulsory, 2003
   4.2 Water levels rose; salinity of coastal wells fell

ABBREVIATIONS USED: NE - north-east; Oct - October; Dec - December

SUMMARY

Tamil Nadu's water problem is one of storage rather than rainfall. The north-east monsoon delivers heavy rain between October and December, but most of it runs off into the sea. Traditional temple tanks and ooranis once caught this rain and recharged the surrounding wells. As these tanks were built over or silted up, borewells replaced them and groundwater was pumped faster than it could be replenished. Chennai's compulsory rainwater harvesting rule of 2003 raised water levels and reduced the salinity of coastal wells, showing that conservation works.

title: General Essay — Reading Habits among Students
instructions: Write an essay of about 150 words on 'The Declining Reading Habit among Students'. Use a clear introduction, two or three body paragraphs with reasons and examples, and a conclusion with a suggestion.
sample_answer:
Reading was once the chief pleasure of a student's free hour. Today the same hour belongs to a screen, and the habit of reading a whole book is quietly disappearing.

The first reason is availability. A short video demands nothing of the viewer, while a book asks for patience and attention. When the easier option is always within reach, the harder one is rarely chosen. The second reason is the examination system itself. Students are trained to read guides and question banks, which give answers without giving the pleasure of discovery. What is read for marks alone is forgotten once the marks are obtained.

The loss is real. Reading builds vocabulary, lengthens attention and, most importantly, allows a young person to live for a while inside another mind.

The remedy need not be grand. A fixed twenty minutes each day, a small class library, and a teacher who reads aloud with enjoyment can restore in a year what neglect has taken away.

title: General Essay — Social Media: Boon or Bane
tamil_title: பொதுக் கட்டுரை — சமூக ஊடகம்: நன்மையா தீமையா
instructions: Write a balanced essay of about 150 words on 'Social Media: Boon or Bane'. Present both sides fairly before stating your own view.
sample_answer:
Few inventions have divided opinion as sharply as social media. To some it is the greatest democratiser of our time; to others, a thief of attention and peace.

The case in its favour is strong. A student in a village can now hear a lecture from a professor she will never meet. Farmers check prices before they load their lorries. During floods and cyclones, rescue has reached people because a message travelled faster than an official order.

The case against it is equally serious. The same speed carries rumour as efficiently as news. Attention is fragmented, sleep is shortened, and young people measure their worth against edited versions of other people's lives.

My own view is that the fault lies less in the tool than in the absence of limits. Used for thirty deliberate minutes, social media is a library and a marketplace. Used without limit, it becomes the master rather than the servant.

title: Story Expansion from Hints (Part IV)
instructions: Expand the following hints into a readable story and give it a suitable title. Add a moral. HINTS: A thirsty crow — flies far — finds a pitcher — water very low — cannot reach — sees pebbles — drops them one by one — water rises — drinks — flies away happily.
sample_answer:
TITLE: WHERE THERE IS A WILL, THERE IS A WAY

It was a burning afternoon in May, and a crow had been flying since morning in search of water. Every pond he passed had dried into cracked mud, and his throat had grown so parched that he could hardly caw.

At last, in the courtyard of a deserted house, he saw a pitcher. His heart lifted, and he flew down at once. But when he looked inside, his hope sank: the water lay far below, barely covering the bottom, and however far he stretched his beak, he could not reach it.

He was about to fly away when he noticed a heap of small pebbles nearby. An idea came to him. He picked up a pebble, dropped it into the pitcher, and went back for another. Again and again he did this, and slowly, with each pebble, the water crept upward.

At last it rose to the neck of the pitcher. The crow drank deeply, ruffled his feathers, and flew away in the cool of the evening.

MORAL: Patience and presence of mind can solve what strength alone cannot.

title: Prose Paragraph Answer (Part IV)
instructions: Answer in a paragraph of about 120 words: 'The author's grandmother was a woman of quiet strength.' Justify this statement with reference to 'The Portrait of a Lady'.
sample_answer:
The grandmother in Khushwant Singh's 'The Portrait of a Lady' shows her strength not in protest but in acceptance. When the family moved to the city and the author began attending an English school, she lost her place as his teacher and companion. She did not complain. She simply withdrew to her spinning wheel, her prayers and her sparrows, and made a full life out of what remained.

Her strength is equally visible in her disapproval. She objected to the music lessons at the English school and to the absence of scripture in it, and she said so once, plainly, and never argued again.

Even her death is an act of will. Knowing her end was near, she stopped speaking, lay down, and told her beads until she died. The silent grief of the thousands of sparrows around her body is the author's final proof of the quiet power she held over every living thing near her.

title: Poetry Paragraph Answer (Part IV)
instructions: Answer in a paragraph of about 120 words: How does Gabriel Okara contrast the past and the present in the poem 'Once Upon a Time'?
sample_answer:
Gabriel Okara builds the whole poem on a contrast between a sincere past and a hollow present, and he draws it through small, physical details rather than abstract statements.

In the past, people laughed with their hearts and with their eyes. In the present they laugh only with their teeth, while their ice-block-cold eyes search behind the speaker's shadow. Once, a handshake was warm and came from the heart; now hands search empty pockets while the mouth speaks politely.

The same reversal marks the words of welcome. 'Feel at home' and 'Come again' were once invitations; now they are formulas, and the door is shut on the second visit.

Most painfully, the father admits that he has himself learnt this falseness, wearing an office face, a street face and a host face. The contrast therefore ends not in accusation but in confession, as he asks his son to teach him how to laugh sincerely once more.

title: Compering Script for a School Function

title: Report Writing — A School Event
instructions: You are the Secretary of the Science Club. Write a report of about 100 words on the Science Exhibition held in your school last week, for publication in the school magazine.
sample_answer:
SCIENCE EXHIBITION HELD AT GOVERNMENT HIGHER SECONDARY SCHOOL, ERODE

By R. Suresh, Secretary, Science Club

A two-day Science Exhibition was held in our school on 12 and 13 August 2025 in the school auditorium. It was inaugurated by Dr. A. Ramesh, Professor of Physics, Government Arts College, Erode.

Sixty-four models prepared by students of Classes IX to XII were displayed under four sections: energy, environment, health and agriculture. A working model of a rainwater harvesting system by the students of Class XI attracted particular attention and was judged the best exhibit.

About nine hundred visitors, including students from six neighbouring schools, attended over the two days. The Principal distributed the prizes at the valedictory function and announced that the exhibition would be made an annual event.

title: Speech Writing — Importance of Discipline
instructions: Write a short speech of about 110 words to be delivered at the school assembly on 'The Importance of Discipline in Student Life'.
sample_answer:
Respected Principal, dear teachers and my dear friends, a very good morning to all of you.

I have been asked to speak this morning on the importance of discipline in student life.

Discipline is often mistaken for punishment. It is not. Discipline is simply the habit of doing what needs to be done, whether or not one feels like doing it that morning. The student who studies for one hour every day, without waiting for the examination to frighten him, has discipline.

All the great achievers we admire had this quality. Dr. Kalam rose at four to study. Mary Kom trained while her family opposed her.

Friends, talent is distributed unequally, but discipline is available to every one of us. Let us begin today, with one small habit kept faithfully.

Thank you.

title: Describing a Picture or Scene
instructions: Describe a busy morning scene at a railway station in about 80 words. Use the present tense and appeal to more than one sense.
sample_answer:
It is half past seven, and the Madurai Junction is at its busiest. The board rattles as it changes, and a metallic voice announces the arrival of the Vaigai Express on platform three.

A porter in a red shirt threads his way through the crowd with two suitcases balanced on his head. Near the tea stall, steam rises from a row of glasses, and the smell of coffee mixes with the sharper smell of engine oil.

A young mother holds her son firmly by the wrist as the train slides in. For a moment the whole platform moves together, and then, just as suddenly, it is quiet again.
